scope: CPU finite-vocabulary semantic audit; no training implementation or GPU benchmark
questions: Does the fixed-index backward of a KL value estimator match the intended KL gradient under its actual proposal?
Does MOPD live-center residual share the BPO population objective while retaining a distinct per-action gradient?
Do stale proposals or coarse centers invalidate the full-center equivalence?

criteria.distinct_per_action_gradient: Report the difference rather than requiring equality

kl_backward_audit.implementation: AST extraction of actual MD-OPD core_algos.py kl_penalty and kl_penalty_forward; torch autograd with detached enumeration weights

proposal_sweep.distribution_generation: Three independent torch.randn(9, generator=seeded_generator, dtype=float64).softmax(-1) per case, in student/teacher/behavior order

mopd_bpo_audit.implementation: AST extraction of actual MOPD residual/floor functions; actual MirrorOPD production cache/loss and independent token_inner.bpo_loss; state terms exactly enumerated
mopd_bpo_audit.reduction: Same detached action measure in each comparison; token aggregation supplied for the mathematical audit, not a test of distributed agg_loss
mopd_bpo_audit.scale: MOPD residual value/expected gradient = 2*eta times exact BPO

coarse_center.singleton_tail_note: In this three-action example K=2 gives a singleton tail and recovers exact centers; this is not a general partial-K equivalence

existing_reference_checks: PYTHONPATH=src uv run --with torch --with numpy python tests/test_mdpo_eta_limits.py
PYTHONPATH=src uv run --with torch --with numpy python tests/test_upstream_opd_semantics.py
PYTHONPATH=src uv run --with torch --with numpy python tests/test_opd_baselines.py
reproduction.note: The listed existing tests corroborate identities. The 200-case sweep is defined above and was run as an inline CPU audit, not added as a production test or benchmark suite. MOPD values here retain the reported float32 precision.
